page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction set extensions including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA.

The system is provisioned with 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation that categorizes it distinctly within memory-heavy tiers. Local storage features an integrated 161 GB solid-state drive, eliminating reliance on network storage for temporary files and local swap. It features no discrete GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard Azure virtual network routing configurations for internet egress and ingress.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate typical mid-range single-core capability paired with modest parallel compute capacity. Single-threaded metrics such as Geekbench single-core (1200.0) and gzip compression throughput (24.1 GB/sec) place in the average tier, while multi-threaded compute results, including PassMark CPU (4396.28) and stress-ng multi-core (3702.46), register in the lower quarter of tested instances. Memory bandwidth metrics record 27.67 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 21.69 GB/sec for uncached writes, reflecting standard DDR4 operational boundaries.

Cost efficiency is centered around the favorable memory-to-vCPU ratio and the inclusion of bundled high-speed local solid-state storage. Workloads constrained by RAM capacity rather than raw compute cycles achieve balanced utilization. The architecture fits relational databases, enterprise applications, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, and staging pipelines requiring local temporary disk performance alongside extensive memory capacity.
